articleBlocks: Cheese, Wheat, and Lettuce can make the board feel like food preparation at first, which is the main trap.
Documents already strains that theory, but Guitar is the clue that really breaks it.
Once 'shredding on guitar' comes into view, the board stops being about one food category and becomes about the shared action word shredded.
After that, shredded cheese, Shredded Wheat, shredded lettuce, and shredded documents all line up naturally.
The answer was Things that can be shredded.
This puzzle works because it mixes literal food prep, office destruction, and musical slang under one connector.
fullAnalysis: Cheese, Wheat, and Lettuce can make the board feel like food preparation at first, which is the main misread.
Documents already strains that theory, but the board becomes much clearer once Guitar appears in the right way.
Guitar is the turning clue because shredding on guitar is a familiar figurative use of the same word, which proves the board is about shredding itself rather than about food.
That shift makes shredded cheese, Shredded Wheat, shredded lettuce, and shredded documents all feel like natural members of the same answer.
The answer was Things that can be shredded.
The board is satisfying because one clue forces you to allow both literal and figurative uses of the same action.
solutionNarrative: Cheese and Lettuce pulled me toward a kitchen answer early, and Wheat almost kept me there. Documents made that theory wobble, but not enough to fully replace it.
Guitar solved the puzzle. Once I let 'shredding' work as a musical verb, the whole board became about what can be shredded rather than about where the clues belong.

lessons.title: One figurative clue can unlock four literal ones
lessons.body: A board may look literal until one clue proves the same word can operate metaphorically too.

lessons.title: Outliers are often the best clue, not the worst one
